documents.source_label: match_0185 target match — continuous broadcast and scorer desk audio
documents.text:
Brookside Training Oval has that subdued, close-to-the-action sound today: a thin crowd, fielders' calls carrying cleanly, and every scrape of a spike audible near the microphones. Tidehaven chose to bat, but the decision begins badly. Noah Vance goes straight through Harvey Lane on the second ball. The director shows the delivery again from behind the arm, then once more from square, yet those are three pictures of one wicket, not three separate events. The board stays at no run for one down.

Miles Sharp joins Rohan Blake. A wide gets Tidehaven moving before Vance bowls Sharp at 1.1. Again the replay lingers: seam upright, the ball coming back, off stump disturbed. The commentary team repeats the dismissal when the next batter walks in, but the scorebook has only the second wicket to enter. Rohan and captain Nolan Reed then try to slow the collapse. The live card briefly puts Rohan on nine during their time together. That figure is repeated on air when the camera returns from a crowd shot, so it sounds settled for a moment.

There is a pause while the ball is returned and the field is reset. Reed taps the crease and Rohan looks towards the pavilion, apparently waiting for the card to catch up. The commentators fill the gap with a description of how little pace is required when the ball is already moving. One voice quotes the number on the lower-third graphic; another says the scorer appears to be checking it. Neither comment marks a fresh scoring event. The sound bed continues with the bowler walking back and the keeper calling encouragement, while the uncertain graphic remains on screen longer than the evidence supporting it.

The scorers are still checking the running sequence. One apparent run originally attached to Rohan did not come from his bat; it belongs in the wide column. Nothing is removed from Tidehaven's team score, only the ownership changes. The old nine beside Rohan's name is withdrawn. When the stand is closed, its ten runs include Reed's one and one extra; Rohan owns the remainder. That decomposition matters more than the cached graphic still visible on a monitor in the commentary box.

The correction arrives conversationally rather than as a formal bulletin. The lead commentator first notices that Rohan's personal tally has stepped back while the team score has stayed still. His partner explains why: the scorer has changed attribution, not erased a delivery. The production desk then shows the earlier running sequence again, which briefly puts the outdated figure beside the corrected discussion. Viewers hear both states within the same minute. The durable clue is the accounting relationship among the closed stand, Reed's contribution and the extra, together with the explicit withdrawal of the old personal figure.

Vance finds Rohan's edge, Arlo Finch takes the catch, and the third wicket is recorded at 11 in the sixth over. Nolan is then bowled at 7.3 with Tidehaven on 12. The wicket package replays Nolan's dismissal later and an automated strip momentarily adds another mark beside Vance. The scorer waves that away: it is the same Nolan Reed wicket being shown again. Vance's distinct victims are Lane, Sharp, Blake and Reed. He has not gained another simply because television revisited the last one.

The camera follows Vance past his teammates and then returns to the broken stumps. From the second angle, Reed's dismissal is introduced with the present tense—'he goes through him'—even though the next batter is already taking guard. A highlights ribbon also places Lane and Sharp beside the new clip. The sequence compresses separate moments from Vance's spell into one package, but the names provide the identity key: Lane, Sharp, Blake and Reed are the completed dismissals. The extra mark that appeared during the package has no new batter, no new ball and no place in the fall-of-wicket sequence.

Caleb Frost and Owen Marsh inherit 12 for four. Their progress is slow enough that every extra feels conspicuous. The stand ledger assigns two runs to Caleb and three to extras. Owen's own number is left for the book to reconcile rather than announced immediately. The pair are separated when Arjun Wells bowls Owen at 13.2. The ground screen first flashes 25 for five, and the broadcaster reads it out before the operator catches up with the scoring desk. One run in that display has duplicated an earlier wide. The total rolls back by one, so the fifth wicket is fixed at 24, not 25, on the second ball of the fourteenth over.

For a moment Owen stays at the crease and looks towards the umpire, more in disappointment than appeal, before turning away. Wells celebrates with the close fielders while the score ribbon and the ground board disagree. The on-air team does not immediately choose between them. They describe the bowled dismissal, wait for the scorer's light, and then note the downward movement on the larger board. The earlier higher state survives in the spoken record because it was read aloud, but the later state connects properly to the innings that follows. No batter returns and no wicket is rescinded.

That also settles two connected entries. The partnership began at 12 and ended at the corrected 24, so its size comes from the distance between those states. Within it Caleb supplied two and the extras supplied three; Owen supplied what remains. The same answer must satisfy both the team-score boundary and the contribution ledger. A later replay of Owen's gate opening does not start or end another partnership.

Wells continues to work through the order. Dylan Pierce is bowled with the total unmoved at 24. Caleb, after making two, is leg before to Wells at 26. Theo Grant is the exception in this sequence: Ben Cole catches him from Elias Grant's bowling at 30, so that dismissal belongs to Elias, not to Wells. Wells then bowls Arun Cole at 35 and returns to bowl Vikram Holt. His credited list is Caleb Frost, Owen Marsh, Dylan Pierce, Arun Cole and Vikram Holt. Each name is counted once and Theo stays in Elias Grant's column.

This is where the cadence of the broadcast becomes deceptive. Wells is discussed through almost the whole collapse, even when Grant is actually operating. The analysts compare release points, the director cuts between Wells waiting near the boundary and Grant beginning his approach, and Theo's catch is replayed while Wells is back in frame. The dismissal sentence itself remains decisive: Cole catches Theo from Grant. Later references to Wells 'running through the order' are summaries of the spell around it, not a reassignment of that wicket. The bowling card must follow credited dismissals rather than whichever bowler dominates the surrounding conversation.

Kian Stone is left at the other end. The ninth wicket had fallen at 35 and the last pair add one. Holt's dismissal arrives on the third legal ball of the twenty-first over. For several seconds the strip says 37 all out, carrying forward the same duplicated wide that had polluted the earlier screen. The innings operator removes it before the players leave: one run since the ninth wicket, ten wickets gone, and 20 complete overs plus three legal deliveries. The stale 37 is no longer an admissible state.

Stone waits near the crease while the fielders shake hands with Holt. The commentary booth initially treats the large screen as conclusive, then notices that the scorers below are still comparing sheets. There is no additional run after Holt is bowled and no extra delivery hidden during the handshake footage. The correction is visible as the board drops, while the legal-ball marker stays on the third ball of the over. That combination distinguishes a scoring rollback from a change to the over count. The terminal innings state must preserve both the corrected runs and the unchanged delivery position.

The extra ledger is scattered across the afternoon's checks. Vance's spells contain four wides; Wells's contain six wides and one no-ball; Ben Cole adds two more wides, while Elias Grant contributes neither a wide nor a no-ball. The innings also contains one leg-bye and no byes. The early live card's aggregate of seventeen is mentioned again during the interval, but it cannot coexist with those final components. The scorer's categories—twelve wides, one no-ball, one leg-bye, zero byes—are the state that survives.

During the interval, the presenters revisit the collapse without reading a finished scorecard. A touchscreen still holds the first live-card aggregate in one corner. Beside it, the scorer's delivery categories are discussed bowler by bowler, and their sum does not support the old aggregate. The panel also replays Rohan's attribution change, explaining that moving a run from the batter to wides altered the personal line while preserving the team total. These are connected corrections: the same run must not be removed from the innings once as a batting adjustment and again as an extra adjustment.

Ridgefield therefore chase one more than Tidehaven's corrected terminal state. Arlo Finch opens with Ben Cole, and the chase has an untidy early episode. From Owen Marsh, a ball is taken in the field and the first shout is 'gone', but the front-foot signal cancels it. That apparent catch produces no dismissal and no bowler wicket. Ben remains at the crease. The broadcast cuts back to the incident later; the second showing does not revive the cancelled wicket.

Ben exchanges a few words with Arlo and marks guard again. Owen walks back slowly, looking at the crease on his way, while the umpire keeps the no-ball signal clear long enough for the scorer to acknowledge it. The commentators debate the shot and the field placement, then a replay restages the catch from a tighter angle. Nothing in that analysis overturns the umpire. The batter continuing at the crease is the state confirmation. Any extraction that keeps the shouted catch while ignoring the no-ball would create a wicket that the subsequent sequence cannot accommodate.

The valid breakthrough comes at 1.5. Ben attacks Owen again, Rohan Blake holds the catch, and this time the delivery is legal. Ben's seven, Arlo's ten and one extra have carried the opening pair to 18. The wicket is entered once. A slow-motion sequence returns to Rohan's catch twice while Noah Vance walks in, but both replays refer to the legal dismissal at 1.5. Owen's column contains the cancelled no-ball chance and the later valid catch; only the latter earns him a wicket.

The similarity between the two moments is exactly what makes the sequence awkward in audio. Both involve Owen, Ben and a catch; one is followed by Ben resetting, the other by Ben leaving. The director places them side by side to compare the strokes. A commentator says Owen has 'finally got him', which links the legal dismissal back to the cancelled chance without creating a pair of wickets. Rohan's celebration and Noah's arrival belong only to the later ball. The continuing innings supplies the temporal boundary that the repeated names alone do not.

Noah and Arlo complete the chase. Their portion starts from 18 for one. Noah contributes two, Arlo contributes another nine after the ten he made in the opening stand, and eight extras travel with the pair. Those are consecutive stands: Arlo's ten and nine should be accumulated, while the repeated footage around Ben's wicket should not be treated as another scoring passage. The second stand's internal ledger and the change in the team total lead to the same number.

Arlo's innings is discussed in fragments rather than announced as a finished line. At the fall of Ben's wicket the booth recalls what he supplied to the opening stand. Near the finish, a separate graphic isolates what he has added alongside Noah. A replay of an earlier scoring shot sits between those references, but the replay carries no new partnership and no new contribution. The two ledger fragments occur on opposite sides of a real wicket boundary, so they must be accumulated. Noah's contribution and the extras then account for the remainder of the unbroken stand.

The target is reached on the third legal ball of the fourth over, with no second batter dismissed. The terminal board therefore has the target value, the single legitimate wicket, three full overs and three further legal deliveries. Arlo is still there; his completed personal score is recovered by joining his contribution from each stand. Noah is also unbeaten. Ridgefield have won by nine wickets, and Vance's opening spell plus his part in the chase earns him player of the match.

The final pictures linger on Vance and Finch walking towards the pavilion while the commentators move between the opening collapse and the brief chase. They replay Vance's early wickets, return to Ben's legal dismissal, and mention the scorer's corrections without presenting a clean row-by-row summary. Crowd sound rises and falls under those callbacks, making old events feel current again. The final broadcast does not recite a full card: the score has to be rebuilt by retaining valid events, discarding replayed ones, separating cancelled appeals from completed dismissals, and carrying every scorer correction through the connected batting, bowling, partnership and wicket states.

documents.source_label: match_0106 target match — continuous broadcast and scorer desk audio
documents.text:
Brookhaven Cricket Oval has that washed, late-afternoon brightness now, and Coral Bay Tides Women have put Meadowridge Spirits Women in. Sienna Park begins with the field up. The opening pair do not look entirely comfortable, but the scoring is untidy rather than absent: a few runs from the bat, a few that the scorer keeps in the extras column, and the board moving often enough to keep everyone checking it.

Elena Cross is the busier of the two. The live graphic briefly gives her eleven, though the scorer beside us is waving at the production desk and asking them to hold that figure. Mira Vale has supplied three during the opening association, and the stand ledger contains five extras. Keep those components in mind; the partnership closes at eighteen when Aila Rowan straightens one and bowls Elena on the final ball of the fourth over. The replay comes twice, first from front-on and then from behind the bowler. It is the same dismissal both times, of course, even though the second replay lands on screen just as the wicket icon flashes again.

A correction from the scoring position: Elena's live-card figure of eleven is withdrawn. They are reconciling the batter columns against that opening stand—eighteen in all, three to Mira and five outside the bat. The scorecard should follow the component ledger, not the first television strip.

Tara Quinn arrives and tries to move the innings along. She makes seven in the next stand, Mira contributes another two, and there are two extras. Maris Vale takes Tara's catch from Aila's bowling at 5.5. A few moments later the director rolls Elena's earlier bowled dismissal while the commentators are talking about Aila's new-ball spell. That old footage must not be counted as another wicket; Aila's distinct entries so far are Elena bowled and Tara caught.

Rowan Hayes joins Mira. Their short association contains four to Rowan, three to Mira and three extras. Nia Brooke traps Mira lbw at 7.5, the total having moved from twenty-nine at the previous wicket to thirty-nine at the third. The first feed briefly attached that lbw to Aila because her spell graphic was still on screen. The scorer has rejected that attribution: Nia delivered the ball, and the dismissal belongs in Nia's column.

There is a short break while the square-leg official checks the ball and the fielders take drinks near the rope. The broadcast uses the pause to show Tara's catch, then Elena's bowled dismissal, then Tara's catch again from a wider camera. The pictures make Aila appear to strike three times, though only two distinct batters are involved. Back live, Rowan scratches her guard, Nora points toward the sight screen, and the old replay label disappears only as the bowler turns. It is exactly the sort of broadcast overlap that makes the event sequence look denser than the scorebook.

Now comes the substantial part of the innings. Rowan and Nora Finch settle into a rhythm which looks much calmer than the first seven overs. The raw stand strip flashes fifty-nine at one point. Nobody in the box signs it off. The batting ledger assigns seventeen to Rowan and twenty-nine to Nora during this partnership, while the extras ledger assigns twelve to the same interval. The scorers say those three components are controlling; the larger live number was a one-run duplication that entered while a no-ball sequence was being replayed.

Nora's twenty-nine in this stretch matters beyond the partnership. Her final batting score will have to be carried forward through several later stands, and there is no reliable single end-of-innings strip for her. Rowan is bowled by Celeste Reed at 15.3. The previous state was thirty-nine for three, and this completed association supplies the entire increment to the fourth-wicket state. The screen takes a moment to catch up, first retaining the old wicket count and then moving to four down. Use the addition and the delivery marker rather than that lagging intermediate picture.

The crowd response arrives before the graphics package. Celeste is already walking back toward her mark when the main board finally changes its wicket column. One commentator begins to quote the obsolete stand number, stops in the middle of the sentence, and hands back to the ball-by-ball voice. The analyst instead talks about Rowan's patience and Nora's placement without offering another total. At ground level, the scorers are still comparing the partnership card with the over sheet, so the absence of an immediate spoken correction is not confirmation of the first display.

The Rowan wicket is Celeste's first distinct dismissal. A studio voice mistakenly calls it her second, apparently having folded a fielding dismissal from a rehearsal graphic into the analysis. There has been no such earlier credited wicket for her in this innings. The official dismissal sequence will settle the column as the innings proceeds.

Lena Moss now accompanies Nora. Lena contributes four, Nora six, and the partnership receives four extras before Lena is run out by Emilia Shaw. The crucial scoring distinction is immediately repeated on air: run out, no bowler's wicket. A provisional bowling strip nevertheless adds Lena to Celeste's column because Celeste had delivered during the passage. That strip is withdrawn. Celeste receives no credit for the run out.

Jade Sinclair is next and lasts two balls, both scoreless. Celeste bowls her. This stand adds nothing; it is a new wicket event, not a replay of Rowan's. Nora has not added to her own tally during those two balls.

Pippa Lane's stay is more productive. Pippa contributes six, Nora two and the stand contains one extra before Nia Brooke bowls Pippa at 18.5. Nora's score therefore continues from her earlier twenty-nine by adding six with Lena, nothing with Jade and two here. The calculation is still unfinished because she remains at the crease.

Ivy Stone joins her for the penultimate completed stand. Ivy supplies five, Nora four, and one extra makes the partnership ten. Bella Marsh takes the catch from Celeste's bowling at 19.5, removing Nora. That is Celeste's third distinct credited dismissal in the live sequence: Rowan bowled, Jade bowled, Nora caught. The earlier four-wicket flash had improperly included Lena's run out and is no longer valid.

Nora's completed batting figure is not read out cleanly. It can be recovered from her non-overlapping partnership contributions: twenty-nine with Rowan, six with Lena, zero with Jade, two with Pippa and four with Ivy. Her catch ends her innings, so the sum stops there. Ivy and Clara Bell then collect two from the final ball—one to Ivy and one extra—taking Meadowridge through the full twenty overs at 132 for eight.

The extras panel is also being rebuilt. The scorer confirms two byes and four leg-byes. The illegal-delivery columns finish with five no-balls and eighteen wides. An early feed had displayed thirty-two extras, but that number has been pulled; it does not equal the four final category totals and was generated before three duplicated penalty entries were removed. The innings rate shown at close is 6.60.

During the interval the cameras stay with the ground staff and the two captains rather than putting a full card on screen. A commentator revisits Nora's late dismissal, but the clip begins with Ivy already on strike and supplies no new scoring event. Another panel briefly shows the withdrawn extras aggregate before being covered by a venue graphic. The on-air team notices it and warns that the number came from the uncorrected live feed. The chase begins without a clean visual recap of every final batting line.

Coral Bay's chase begins with Jade Sinclair operating to Aila Rowan. Aila survives three balls and is bowled on the fourth, with the total at one. The replay remains on screen while Nia Brooke takes guard, then Jade traps Nia lbw on the very next legal delivery. One run for two wickets. The gallery cuts back to Aila's dismissal just as the lbw is confirmed; the pictures are out of order, but these are two separate wickets, one bowled and one leg-before.

Maris Vale and Emilia Shaw try to absorb the pressure. Maris eventually makes two in thirteen balls. Their stand is made up of one to Emilia, two to Maris and one extra. Jade then bowls Maris at 3.6. A later slow-motion package again shows Aila's off stump disturbed, labelled only as “Sinclair strikes”; it is an old clip from the opening over. Jade's wicket ledger should contain the three distinct batters just described, without counting that replay as a fourth.

Emilia is joined by Lara Holt. Each batter adds one and there are no extras before Nora Finch catches Lara from Tara Quinn at 6.2. The total is seven for four. Emilia's contribution ledger now has one from the Maris stand and one from the Lara stand; she is batting on, so neither a provisional aggregate nor the screen's rounded graphic should be treated as final.

Sienna Park gives Emilia the longest resistance of the chase. The partnership feed first announces eighteen, then pauses. The official components are four to Sienna, nine to Emilia and four extras. The scorer explains the surplus live run: a wide from the previous over had been carried into this stand a second time. The eighteen is retracted and the component sum controls. Ivy Stone bowls Sienna on the first ball of the thirteenth over.

The fielders gather around Ivy, but the television remains on the previous partnership graphic while Faye Turner prepares. A replay angle shows Sienna's stumps, cuts to Emilia at the non-striker's end, then returns to the same broken stumps after the next delivery has already been bowled. The commentator corrects the chronology aloud: the first pictures belong to Sienna, live play has moved on, and the batter now facing is Faye. No additional run or wicket should be inferred from the repeated celebration.

That passage also supplies the largest partnership of the Coral Bay innings, but the sequence immediately becomes chaotic. Faye Turner is bowled by Ivy two balls later without scoring. Emilia contributes nothing during that stand. Bella Marsh is then bowled by Ivy at the end of the over; Bella contributes nothing, Emilia again contributes nothing, and one extra separates the wickets. Three distinct wickets belong to Ivy across the sequence, while the television repeatedly reuses the Sienna replay between deliveries.

Celeste Reed adds one with the bat, Emilia adds one and there is one extra before Rowan Hayes catches Celeste from Tara Quinn at 14.2. Ruth Elms then stays long enough to add three; Emilia contributes six and one extra completes a ten-run stand. Mira Vale bowls Ruth at 16.5, leaving Coral Bay at thirty-eight for nine.

The lower-third graphic now claims Emilia has twenty. The scorer will not certify it. Her partnership contributions to this point are one with Maris, one with Lara, nine with Sienna, zero with Faye, zero with Bella, one with Celeste and six with Ruth. Priya Cove is the last partner, so Emilia's final amount still depends on the last stand rather than on that provisional twenty.

Priya finds a boundary from her first ball and finishes with five from the stand. Emilia contributes one more, with no extras. The partnership adds six to the state at the ninth wicket. On ball 17.4 Emilia drives Mira Vale and Jade Sinclair takes the catch; she is the tenth batter dismissed. The final fall is obtained by carrying the six-run stand forward from thirty-eight for nine and pairing it with that delivery marker.

Emilia's stand ledger can now be closed. Across her eight partnerships the contributions are one, one, nine, zero, zero, one, six and one. The scorer rejects the earlier television twenty when those non-overlapping pieces are added. Priya remains not out.

For the chase's extras audit, the stand-by-stand entries, in order, are one, zero, one, zero, four, zero, one, one, one and zero. They cover every partnership from Aila's opening stand through the final dismissal, so no separate remainder is needed. Meadowridge's eighty-eight-run win is confirmed, and Jade Sinclair is named player of the match after her new-ball burst and the final catch.

documents.source_label: match_0178 target match — continuous broadcast and scorer desk audio
documents.text:
The broadcast from South Meridian Institute Ground has had an awkward afternoon with the scoring ribbon, so every number on screen needs to be treated as a state at that moment, not automatically as a final entry. Shoreline Rangers chose to bat, and the early passage is easiest to follow through the fall of wickets. Leo Marsh was the first man out at 62 after 8.4 overs, caught by Aiden Scott from Zane Cooper. Two legal balls later Rory Blake was bowled by the same bowler without the score moving. The replay director shows Rory's dismissal twice: first from behind the arm and then from square leg. The second showing is a replay, not another delivery and not another wicket.

Finn Archer's opening phase is being reconstructed from the stand book because the live card has not settled. He supplied 39 during the opening partnership with Leo. Rory's two-ball stay produced no run for either partner, so Finn added nothing in that tiny second-wicket stand. Against the next partnership, with Miles Carter, Finn supplied another 35. He then did not score in the brief stand with Dylan Vale before being caught by Arin Wells from Miles Benton. The first television card had Finn at 75, and that number returns during a later highlights package. The scorer is clear that one run already included in the team total had sat in the wrong personal column. It leaves Finn's bat column and does not become an extra run for the side. The contribution ledger remains 39, then 0, then 35, then 0.

The Finn Archer-Miles Carter stand is another place where the pictures run ahead of the book. It begins with Shoreline on 62 for two. Miles contributes 36, Finn contributes 35, and five runs in the interval belong to extras. A green caption briefly calls the partnership 77. That caption has pulled the first run of the following stand backward across the wicket boundary. The scoring desk separates it again. Miles Carter is caught at 23.4, the third wicket, and the incoming pair starts from 138 for three. When the replay of the stand appears ten overs later, it is the same partnership being discussed; it must not be added a second time.

Finn's dismissal brings Dylan Vale into the longer middle-innings account. Dylan's first contribution is four in the short association before Finn goes. He adds 13 alongside Connor Wells, nine alongside Evan Price and 37 alongside Noah Grant. A running extra is initially painted beside Dylan's name, producing a momentary 64 on the television strip. The scorer moves that run away from the batter. Nothing new has happened on the field during that graphical change. Dylan's contribution entries stay four, thirteen, nine and thirty-seven, and the later highlights repeat those components without creating any extra runs.

Zane Cooper's bowling figure is also contaminated by the replay loop. His valid dismissal entries are Leo Marsh caught, Rory Blake bowled and Connor Wells bowled. The automated live card once shows five. One of the additions comes from treating the second camera angle of Rory's wicket as a fresh entry, and the old cached card keeps that inflated figure. Only those distinct names belong against Zane in the dismissal ledger. Finn Archer is not one of them; his wicket belongs to Miles Benton.
